overview: Transition Raphael from brute-force execution to surgical, phantom-like operation. Integrate OPSEC, rate limiting, WAF evasion, and strict scope adherence into the existing cognitive loop without modifying D-series core.
governing_principles: CapabilityBroker remains the sole authority for all execution decisions
RateLimiter and ScopeParser are extensions of Broker — not separate components
Fail closed: ambiguous scope status => DENY
Do not modify D-series core cognitive loop (Planner, WorldModel, HypothesisEngine)
All stealth modifications must be reversible for lab testing

spec_sections.name: Strict Scope Parser
spec_sections.defect: CapabilityBroker uses simple CIDR/hostname lists. HackerOne scopes are complex: wildcard domains, exclusions, URL-path scoping, and structured policy documents.
spec_sections.required_change: Implement a dedicated ScopeParser module that ingests structured scope definitions and compiles them into a rigorous authorization policy.
acceptance_criteria: Parse wildcard domains: *.example.com matches any subdomain
Parse exclusion rules: !support.example.com denies that specific host
Parse URL-path scoping: example.com/api/* limits to path prefix
Parse CIDR notation: 10.0.0.0/24
Parse HackerOne JSON export format: in_scope, out_of_scope arrays
Fail closed: if target cannot be definitively classified => DENY
Cache compiled rules for O(1) lookup per authorization check
Export compiled policy as EngagementPolicy.allowed_targets / prohibited_targets

interface.integration: CapabilityBroker.__init__() accepts optional ScopeParser. If provided, is_target_allowed() delegates to ScopeParser instead of raw list matching.

risk_assessment.false_positive: Overly broad wildcard may inadvertently allow out-of-scope subdomain. Mitigation: require explicit wildcard + explicit exclusion pairs.
risk_assessment.false_negative: Complex URL pattern may not match due to normalization differences (e.g., trailing slash). Mitigation: normalize all targets before matching.
risk_assessment.performance: Policy compilation is O(n) at init. Lookup is O(1) amortized via compiled trie.

spec_sections.name: Rate Limiting & Temporal Jitter
spec_sections.defect: AblationRunner executes actions as fast as LLM and tools allow, triggering WAF thresholds.
spec_sections.required_change: Introduce a RateLimiter module into CapabilityBroker. Every authorize_action and authorize_shell_command call must be subject to configurable delay with jitter.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable min_delay (default 5s) and max_delay (default 15s) per action
Random jitter within [min_delay, max_delay] applied before returning authorization
Per-target rate tracking: separate rate limits for each target IP
Global rate limit: max actions per minute/hour across all targets

Shell session keep-alive: heartbeat (empty 
) sent during rate limiter wait to prevent timeout
Rate limit stats exposed via GET /v1/rate-limiter/status
Emergency brake: if >10 DENY in 60s, auto-pause for 300s

methods: authorize_with_delay(target: str, action_type: str) -> tuple[bool, str, float]
interface.integration: CapabilityBroker.propose_action() and authorize_shell_command() call rate_limiter.authorize_with_delay() before returning authorization decision. ShellSession.send_command() sends keepalive during delay.

risk_assessment.false_positive: Excessive delay may cause shell session timeout. Mitigation: keepalive heartbeat maintains session.
risk_assessment.false_negative: Per-target tracking may allow multi-target burst. Mitigation: global rollup counter caps total throughput.
risk_assessment.performance: time.sleep() is blocking. Mitigation: use asyncio.sleep() in async context, threaded sleep in sync.

spec_sections.name: WAF Detection & Fingerprinting
spec_sections.defect: Student proposes static payloads. If WAF blocks them, FalsificationManager records failure and Raphael moves on, missing the vulnerability.
spec_sections.required_change: Before Planner proposes an exploit payload, fingerprint the target's WAF. Store WAF identity in WorldModel. Select WAF-specific encoded payloads.
acceptance_criteria: WAF probe on first encounter: send GET with X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 and check response headers
Detect Cloudflare: Server header, cf-ray header, 403 with '__cf_chl_' in body
Detect AWS WAF: x-amzn-RequestId header, 403 with 'RequestBlocked' body
Detect Akamai: Server: AkamaiGHost, 403 with 'Reference' number
Detect ModSecurity: 406 Not Acceptable, 'ModSecurity' in body
Detect imperva/Incapsula: 'incapsula' in body, 509 Bandwidth Limit
Store WAF type as TARGET_ATTRIBUTE on target entity in WorldModel
Student.technique_proposer() queries WorldModel for WAF type before selecting payload variant
Payload variants indexed by WAF type in STACK_MAP

interface.integration: Student.technique_proposer() calls WAFDetector.fingerprint(target) before generating candidates. Results stored in WorldModel via store_target_attribute(). Planner queries WorldModel for waf_type when scoring exploit candidates.

risk_assessment.false_positive: WAF fingerprint probe may alert defender. Mitigation: probe uses legitimate-looking X-Forwarded-For header; plain GET to /.
risk_assessment.false_negative: WAF may be undetectable or custom. Mitigation: fall back to baseline payloads if no WAF detected; LLM mutation as secondary path.
risk_assessment.performance: Single HTTP request per target at recon phase. Negligible overhead.

spec_sections.name: LLM-Driven Payload Mutation
spec_sections.defect: STACK_MAP contains one payload per technique. If blocked, no fallback.
spec_sections.required_change: If payload blocked by WAF, FalsificationManager signals Student to mutate payload via LLM. Alternative encodings generated and proposed as new Candidates.
acceptance_criteria: FalsificationManager detects WAF block (403/406/509 status code, blocked keywords in response)
FalsificationManager sets falsification.metadata['waf_blocked'] = True
Student module receives waf_blocked signal and calls PayloadMutator
PayloadMutator.mutate() sends original payload + WAF type to LLM with prompt for N alternative encodings
Supported mutation techniques: double URL encoding, case variation, comment insertion (SQL), whitespace obfuscation, hex encoding, base64 wrapping, charset bypass
Returned mutations proposed as new Candidates via existing Candidate proposal path
Max 3 mutation rounds per original payload to prevent infinite loops
Caching: same payload + WAF type returns cached mutations within 5-minute TTL

methods: mutate(original_payload: str, waf_type: str, technique: str) -> list[str]
interface.integration: FalsificationManager.complete_falsification() checks metadata for waf_blocked. If true, calls Student.propose_mutations(original_candidate). Student calls PayloadMutator.mutate() and submits new Candidates to Planner.

risk_assessment.false_positive: LLM may generate invalid/malformed payloads. Mitigation: syntax validation before Candidate proposal; max 3 rounds prevents infinite loops.
risk_assessment.false_negative: LLM may fail to generate effective bypass. Mitigation: fallback to dynamic techniques (time-based, out-of-band) rather than repeated mutation.
risk_assessment.cost: Each LLM mutation call costs tokens. Mitigation: cache mutations per (payload, waf_type) with 5-min TTL.

implementation_order.rationale: Scope safety is the highest priority. Parser must exist before any engagement.
Rate limiting prevents WAF triggering and bans. Must be active before any exploit action.
WAF detection informs payload selection. Must run during recon phase.
Payload mutation is the fallback when initial payloads are blocked. Depends on WAF type from P1-SS-03.

safety_invariants: SI-P1-01: ScopeParser must DENY if target status is ambiguous
SI-P1-02: RateLimiter must never block emergency shutdown (kill -9 style termination)
SI-P1-03: WAF detection probes must not contain exploit payloads
SI-P1-04: Payload mutation must not exceed 3 rounds per original payload
SI-P1-05: CapabilityBroker remains the sole authorization authority
SI-P1-06: All stealth modules log every decision for audit trail
SI-P1-07: RateLimiter keepalive must not execute commands — only send empty newline
